question: When a body of mass m is raised to a height H against gravity, the potential energy of the body is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**increased by an amount mgH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potential energy (PE) is the energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to a reference point, often the Earth.
 
• When a body of mass m is raised to a height H against gravity, the work done against the gravitational force is stored as potential energy.
 
• The formula for gravitational potential energy is PE = m * g * H, where g is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth).
 
• Thus, raising a body of mass m to a height H increases its potential energy by an amount equal to m * g * H.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Force**

 
 
• It is a force that attracts any two objects with mass towards each other.
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy**
 
 
• This is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or state.
 
• It is a form of mechanical energy, alongside kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Principle**
 
 
• This principle states that the work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• In the context of potential energy, work done against gravity is stored as potential energy.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy**
 
 
• This fundamental principle states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• In an ideal system, the total energy remains constant over time.
